# Results — Study 819 (Abnormal-Volume Shock)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Garfinkel
& Sokobin (2006): **unusual trading volume** proxies attention / opinion divergence, so names
printing abnormally high volume go on to earn a **positive subsequent drift**; a long
high-abnormal-volume / short low-abnormal-volume book should earn a positive spread. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month
is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC **+ Volume** (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **standardised abnormal volume** `(V − mean_60) / std_60` (volume vs its own trailing 60-day norm), **averaged over the last 5 days** (formation window), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the top 30%** (high abnormal volume), **short the bottom 30%** (low abnormal volume), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. The
disagreement/attention drift is documented most strongly around **earnings announcements** and
in **smaller, less-covered** names; a 50-mega-cap, all-days survivor panel is exactly where the
effect is most diluted — which is what we find.

## The headline — long-high-avol / short-low-avol spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% abnormal-volume spread (n = **4,083** days,
median 50 names/day):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-avol − short low-avol)** | **+0.55 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+0.54** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.52 |
| high-avol book / low-avol book | +7.44 bps / +6.89 bps (Welch *t* = +0.21) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | +0.13 |

The claimed edge is in the **right direction but statistically absent.** Garfinkel & Sokobin
predict a positive drift on high abnormal volume; the sign here *is* positive (+0.55 bps/day),
but the Newey-West *t* is **+0.54** — indistinguishable from zero. The high-abnormal-volume book
(+7.44 bps) barely out-earns the low-abnormal-volume book (+6.89 bps), a 0.55 bps gap with a
Welch *t* of +0.21. On daily data over 50 liquid mega-caps the attention/disagreement drift
does **not** show up as a tradable cross-sectional spread.

## Placebo — is even the tiny spread a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the abnormal-volume sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+0.55 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.015 bps (0.865) |
| position of observed | ≈ **0.62σ into the right tail** (right-tail p = **0.266**) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed +0.55 bps sits well inside the bulk of the
placebo distribution (p = 0.27), so even the small positive tilt is consistent with a lucky
draw of the sort — there is no signal to speak of.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,949) | −0.48 bps | **−0.40** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +1.49 bps | **+0.94** |

The sign even **flips** between halves (−0.48 bps then +1.49 bps), neither half significant —
the opposite of a stable edge.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +0.55 bps | 2.14 bps | **−1.59 bps** | −1.49 | −0.37 | −4.0%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +0.55 bps | 10.14 bps | **−9.59 bps** | −8.98 | −2.23 | −24.2%/yr |

A +0.55 bps/day gross tilt is dwarfed by the 2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at a mere 1 bp
one-way; the book is net negative at any realistic cost. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "attention shock" that inflates each name's
volume and (with `edge>0`) lifts its forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.27** (sd 1.05) — ≈ N(0,1); \|t\| ≥ 2 in **2/20** (≈ nominal size) |
| planted (`edge = 0.0020`, seed 819) | **+21.64** (Welch *t* = +22.46) |

The detector recovers a *planted* Garfinkel-Sokobin drift overwhelmingly and its null *t* is
distributed ≈ N(0,1) (mean −0.27, sd 1.05, firing at roughly the nominal 5% rate) — so the flat
real-tape result is a genuine absence of the effect on this universe, not a dead engine.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The famous Garfinkel-Sokobin attention/disagreement drift does **not**
  replicate as a tradable cross-sectional spread on 50 liquid US mega-caps. The specified
  long-high-abnormal-volume / short-low book earns **+0.55 bps/day** (NW *t* = **+0.54**) —
  correctly signed but statistically indistinguishable from zero, sitting only 0.62σ into a
  1,000-permutation placebo (p = 0.27) and **flipping sign** across the two eras (−0.40 / +0.94).
  A clean synthetic control (planted *t* = +21.6, null ≈ N(0,1)) confirms the flat result is the
  data, not the engine. The disagreement drift is an earnings-window / small-cap phenomenon that
  is diluted to nothing on an all-days mega-cap panel.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even the right-signed +0.55 bps/day gross tilt is eaten by the
  2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at 1 bp one-way (net −1.59 bps/day), and −9.59 bps/day at
  5 bps. No version of the book survives costs.
